feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. The evidence so far: iteration 0 (symmetric five sensors at y=0.04 m, kp 2.0) and iteration 1 (five sensors at y=0.06 m, kp 3.2, ki 0.15, kd 0.2) all ended off_track, with max_error at the 0.06 m floor and low steering_oscillation (0.07 to 0.16). Iteration 2 (seven sensors at y=0.07 m, wheel_radius 0.035, wheel_track 0.11, kp 4.0, kd 0.3) raised oval progress to about 0.63 and finished 2 of 20 oval trials, but steering_oscillation rose to 0.27 to 0.28 and control_effort to about 8 to 8.5, and s-bend progress stayed at 0.34. So sensing and lookahead were not the limit in iteration 2; overshoot was. Integration work I had to do: scaled the seven sensor weights to x/0.015 to keep the signal sign-correct, kept ki 0.15 for the motor mismatch, and raised kd to 0.4 against overshoot. For the next race: if steering_oscillation falls below 0.27 and max_error still reaches 0.06 m on the s-bend, the wider track is adding damping but turn authority is the limit, so try a moderately higher wheel_track is not the answer; instead try the sensor y, below. If steering_oscillation stays at or above 0.27 with the wider track, the turn response is still too fast and the track should go back toward 0.11 m. If line_loss_events rise at y=0.08 m, the far sensors are losing the tape and the lookahead is too far.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation is still at or above 0.27 on the oval and s-bend, with max_error at 0.06 m: set wheel_track to 0.12 m as a middle value between iteration 2's 0.11 m and this 0.13 m, since iteration 2 showed overshoot at 0.11 m with kp 4.0.

If line_loss_events rise above about 1 per run at y=0.08 m (iteration 2 at y=0.07 m gave 1.2 on the oval and 1.3 on the s-bend): set sensor y to 0.075 m, since the far sensors may be losing the 25 mm tape at maximum lookahead.

If the robot is stable (steering_oscillation below 0.27) but completion_time on the oval stays above 3 s, or completions stay rare: raise wheel_radius to 0.045 m for more ground speed, since iteration 2's 0.035 m wheel gave an oval mean finish time of 1.7 s only in the two finishing runs and most runs stalled off_track.
